nodes.label: Project Constitution v1.3.0
nodes.rationale: Non-negotiable rules that outrank any spec; amendment requires an explicit dated entry so rules cannot be edited silently.

nodes.label: Article I — Purpose and Honest Framing
nodes.rationale: The predecessor README claimed performance the code could not reproduce; overstated claims are the most damaging thing a portfolio project can contain because they are trivially checked. Hence portfolio-only framing and a falsifiable headline question whose negative answer is publishable.

nodes.label: Article II — The Baseline Is Sovereign
nodes.rationale: v0 lost to a one-line baseline on five of six metrics and nobody noticed for four months because the baseline was never computed. An uncomputed baseline is an unfalsifiable claim, so every report must carry it on the same holdout and metrics.

nodes.label: Article III — No Temporal Leakage
nodes.rationale: In v0 `weather_mixed` was the third most important feature and was computed from the actual weather of the race being predicted, inflating every reported metric. Admissibility is therefore defined by whether a value is knowable before race start, and each feature must declare its input availability in code.

nodes.label: III.6 — Modelling Randomness Is Not Knowing the Outcome
nodes.rationale: Supplying an actual outcome does not capture unpredictability, it removes the model's need to handle it. Pre-race rain probability is admissible; whether it actually rained is not. Added so Article III could not be misread as banning stochastic modelling.

nodes.label: Article IV — Chronological Evaluation Only
nodes.rationale: v0's holdout was two races and forty rows, so every metric was indistinguishable from noise in both directions. Random splits leak future into past; the corpus floor is 8 seasons (5 train / 3 holdout) and every metric needs an uncertainty estimate.

nodes.label: IV.2a — Publish the Shortfall, Never Lower the Bar
nodes.rationale: A smaller corpus is a published limitation, never a silent redefinition of the minimum to fit what was collected.

nodes.label: Article V — Probabilities Must Be Calibrated
nodes.rationale: v0's simulator emitted confident-looking win probabilities to four decimal places with no evidence they meant anything. Precision without calibration is decoration.

nodes.label: UNCALIBRATED Render-Layer Label (V.4)
nodes.rationale: v1.2.0 softened the outright display ban to display-with-label because v1.1.0's V.4 directly contradicted FR-705. The label is applied at the rendering layer specifically so that no call site can omit it, and V.5 still bars such numbers from supporting any claim.

nodes.label: Article VI — Reproducibility
nodes.rationale: v0's collection died partway through 2024 and could not resume because per-season checkpoints were written to paths that were never created; four seasons of intended data quietly became one. Hence seeded determinism, incremental resumable collection, and full artifact metadata.

nodes.label: Article VII — Spec-Driven Development
nodes.rationale: Order of work is spec to plan to tasks to code, and every task cites a requirement ID. VII.1a exempts spikes, support code and behaviour-preserving refactors because the rule exists to stop unrequested features accreting, not to make investigation illegal.

nodes.label: Article VIII — Data Provenance and Licensing
nodes.rationale: FastF1's MIT licence covers the software, not Formula 1's timing data, so the repository ships the code to acquire data rather than the data, and avoids trademark use implying affiliation.

nodes.label: Article IX — Human Ratification
nodes.rationale: v1.0.0 mandated spec-to-code order but never required a human to approve the spec, so an agent could author requirements, approve them implicitly by proceeding, and implement against them while satisfying every stated rule. This happened in Phase P0. A rule that permits the thing it exists to prevent is a defective rule, so IX.3 makes author-and-approver separation structural.

nodes.label: Article X — Race Randomness Must Be Modelled, Not Known
nodes.rationale: Article III addressed F1's unpredictability only by prohibition — it said what may not be known and nothing about what must be modelled. Retirements, safety cars and weather swings are part of the phenomenon, so they must be modelled as distributions from prior races only, and no prediction may be a bare point estimate.

nodes.label: Irreducible Noise Floor (X.5)
nodes.rationale: Without a noise floor, a model doing genuinely well against an unpredictable sport is indistinguishable from one doing badly, and the temptation to close that gap with leaked features becomes overwhelming — precisely how v0 went wrong. Model error is therefore interpreted against the floor rather than against zero.

nodes.label: X.1a — Weather's Two Distinct Roles
nodes.rationale: Added in v1.3.0 after the owner observed FR-751..755 never mentioned weather while Article X's own rationale named weather swings as irreducible randomness. As input only a forecast or climatological prior is admissible; as randomness, race-day conditions are a distribution. Observed race weather is inadmissible in both roles.

nodes.label: Grid-Order Baseline (II.1)
nodes.rationale: Predicted finishing position equals starting grid position, computed on the exact same holdout with the exact same metrics; a second naive control such as championship-standings order guards against one baseline being unrepresentative.

nodes.label: Oracle Variant Upper Bound (III.4)
nodes.rationale: Inadmissible but interesting features may be evaluated as an explicitly labelled oracle variant that establishes an upper bound; oracle results may never be reported as the model's performance.

nodes.label: Constitution Amendment Log
nodes.rationale: Versioned trail from v1.0.0 through v1.3.0 recording each change and the owner reasoning behind it, so no rule changes without an attributable justification.

nodes.label: Outstanding Compliance Debt (Phase P0)
nodes.rationale: Phase P0 (commit 920b7c8) executed against an unratified Draft spec, which IX.1 now prohibits. Recorded rather than quietly retro-approved; the work is deletion-only and recoverable at tag v0-vibe-coded, and it does not count as precedent.

nodes.label: Race Result Predictor README
nodes.rationale: Deliberately carries no performance claims yet: the previous README claimed numbers the code could not reproduce, so under Constitution I.3 a claim appears only once it resolves to a committed file in results/.

nodes.label: Phase P1 Blocked Ratification Gate
nodes.rationale: Constitution IX.1 prohibits implementing against a Draft spec; the gate lifts only when the owner has read spec.md in full and ticked its ratification checklist.

nodes.label: The Headline Question
nodes.rationale: Finishing order is largely set by qualifying, so any model competes against a free signal readable off the grid sheet. A negative answer is a valid result and will be published as one.

nodes.label: v0 Audit — Lost to a One-Line Baseline
nodes.rationale: The v0 system ran end to end and looked convincing but lost to the grid baseline on five of six metrics (MAE 3.675 vs 3.550, exact 15.0% vs 17.5%, within-2 42.5% vs 55.0%, top-3 50.0% vs 66.7%; it won only Spearman 0.621 vs 0.569). Root causes were temporal leakage via weather_mixed and a forty-row holdout — process failures, not coding errors.

nodes.label: Structural Controls Preventing Recurrence
nodes.rationale: Each v0 failure is mapped to a control that makes it structurally detectable: derived feature sets (FR-201, D-1), baselines sharing the evaluation code path (FR-304), three-season holdout with bootstrap CIs (FR-501, FR-503), render-layer uncalibrated labelling (FR-701, D-7), per-season checkpointing (FR-102, FR-103), and every figure citing a committed results file (FR-902).

nodes.label: Project Structure Map
nodes.rationale: Constitution, spec (46 functional requirements), plan, tasks, src/f1pred, and committed results — 'read the spec before the code, that is the point of it'.

nodes.label: Data and Licensing Statement
nodes.rationale: FastF1's MIT licence covers the software and not Formula 1's timing data, so the repository ships acquisition code only; the project is a portfolio piece, not a commercial product or betting advice.

nodes.label: Pinned Dependency Set
nodes.rationale: v0 floated every dependency with >= and silently drifted across three major versions; it happened to survive, and that was luck rather than a strategy. Pinned per plan.md §4 (NFR-02), verified latest mutually-compatible set on Python 3.13 with pip check passing, re-verified before each phase.

nodes.label: fastf1 3.8.3 pin
nodes.rationale: Sole data-acquisition dependency; its declared pandas cap governs the rest of the data stack.

nodes.label: pandas <3.0.0 Constraint
nodes.rationale: fastf1 declares pandas<3.0.0. The project arrived in the broken state once already — pandas 3.0.2 was installed over fastf1's cap and sat broken until pip check was run on 2026-08-16, and collection (P1) is the phase that would have hit it. Held at pandas 2.3.3.

nodes.label: pytest 9.1.1 (NFR-03, NFR-04)
nodes.rationale: Absent from v0 entirely, so v0's tests were never runnable.

nodes.label: Committed Results Directory
nodes.rationale: Tracked in version control on purpose: under FR-902 / AC-7 every performance number in documentation must resolve to a file here, and a claim that cannot cite one does not get made. Populated from Phase P3 onward.

nodes.label: Plan 001 — Core Predictor
nodes.rationale: States HOW the spec will be built; every design decision cites the requirement forcing it, and a decision citing no requirement is scope creep to be removed or backed by a new requirement.

nodes.label: Pipeline Architecture Overview
nodes.rationale: FastF1 feeds resumable collection to season parquet, then the features layer acts as the leakage firewall, then models, then evaluation and simulation converge on committed results. The load-bearing idea is the feature registry: leakage is prevented structurally rather than by vigilance.

nodes.label: src/f1pred Module Layout
nodes.rationale: v0 used a bare namespace package with no __init__.py, so `python -m src.cli` worked only from the repo root. A named package is importable, testable, and installable (NFR-02).

nodes.label: D-1 — Feature Registry with Availability Declarations
nodes.rationale: The primary feature set is computed as the PRE_RACE subset of the registry rather than written by hand, so it cannot drift out of sync with reality — the v0 failure mode. Rejected alternative: a hand-maintained allowlist in config.py, which is exactly what v0 had and where weather_mixed sat undetected for four months.

nodes.label: Availability Enum (PRE_RACE / POST_RACE)
nodes.rationale: Machine-readable availability class attached by the @feature decorator; PRE_RACE is admissible in the primary model, POST_RACE reaches only the oracle variant.

nodes.label: D-2 — Two-Layer Leakage Testing
nodes.rationale: A static check asserts no POST_RACE feature reaches the primary matrix; a behavioural check perturbs the target race's outcome and asserts every pre-race feature is unchanged, catching off-by-one rolling-window errors a static check cannot see. A negative control (a deliberately leaky feature that must fail the check) exists because a leakage test that has never failed is not known to work.

nodes.label: D-3 — Baselines Share the Model's Code Path
nodes.rationale: Baselines implement the same Predictor protocol as the model, so evaluation is written once against the protocol and it becomes impossible to evaluate the model on terms the baselines did not face — which is how v0's baseline gap went unnoticed.

nodes.label: Predictor Protocol
nodes.rationale: Single interface `predict(race_frame) -> ranked positions` shared by every baseline and the model, making them interchangeable in evaluation.

nodes.label: D-4 — Chronological Splitting as a First-Class Object
nodes.rationale: A ChronologicalSplit object owns the train/holdout boundary and no function anywhere accepts a test_size float — random splitting is not merely discouraged, the API makes it unexpressible.

nodes.label: D-5 — Bootstrap at Race Granularity
nodes.rationale: Resampling resamples races, not driver-rows, because driver-rows within a race are strongly dependent and row-level bootstrap would produce dishonestly narrow intervals. Deltas are computed within each replicate, preserving model/baseline pairing.

nodes.label: D-6 — Weather Handling Pending OQ-2
nodes.rationale: Actual race weather is POST_RACE and excluded from the primary set, but stays registered so the oracle variant can quantify how much the v0 numbers were inflated — a genuinely interesting result for the write-up.

nodes.label: D-7 — Port the Simulator, Gate It on Calibration
nodes.rationale: v0's race_simulator.py logic is structurally sound and ported largely intact; what is added is the calibration harness and a display gate enforced in the render layer so it cannot be forgotten at a call site.

nodes.label: D-8 — pandas Held at 2.x by fastf1
nodes.rationale: The v0 environment had pandas 3.0.2 over fastf1's <3.0.0 cap so pip check failed and the environment was unsupported — undetected because the only path exercising fastf1 heavily is collection, which never completed. Decision: follow the resolver; a pip-check-clean environment is worth more to a reproducibility-governed project than a major version number. Rejected alternative: dropping fastf1 for the jolpica-f1 REST API, which would invalidate the 365M cache, lose telemetry access, and require rewriting all of P1.

nodes.label: D-9 — Corpus Window Resolved at Run Time
nodes.rationale: ChronologicalSplit receives a CorpusWindow that resolves from what is on disk rather than a literal season list; a season counts as completed when its final round's race date is past, making FR-508's advance automatic and FR-509 structural. Width defaults to 16 (2010-2025 per OQ-6) and is overridable so the recency-versus-volume trade-off can be measured. Rejected alternative: a SEASONS constant, correct for exactly one year and silently wrong afterwards.

nodes.label: D-10 — Regulation Regimes as Declared Data
nodes.rationale: Regime boundaries are a hand-maintained table (2010, 2011, 2014, 2017, 2019, 2022, 2026) because F1's regulation cycle is irregular and nothing in the data announces a reset. Three mechanisms hang off it: regime_id and seasons_since_regime_start as PRE_RACE features, exponential recency weighting where zero decay reproduces uniform weighting exactly, and the relative-feature constraint enforced in the same static scan as leakage. Rejected alternative: change-point detection on lap times — detecting what you already know is complexity with no payoff.

nodes.label: Recency Weighting (exp decay sample_weight)
nodes.rationale: sample_weight = exp(-decay * seasons_ago) passed to XGBoost with decay recorded as a hyperparameter; zero decay reproduces uniform weighting exactly, so the comparison is a parameter sweep rather than a second code path.

nodes.label: Technology Stack and Pinning Policy
nodes.rationale: Python 3.13.5 chosen over 3.14 because the gain does not justify a venv rebuild mid-project; dependencies are pinned rather than floated because v0's >= drift survived on luck, and luck is not a dependency strategy.

nodes.label: Reference Machine (NFR-01)
nodes.rationale: Timing budgets are meaningless without a named machine: Apple Silicon, macOS 25.6, Python 3.13.5, with every results file recording measured wall-clock time so a reader on different hardware can scale rather than guess.

nodes.label: Disposition of v0 Code (Port / Rewrite / Delete)
nodes.rationale: Nothing is deleted for being ugly, only for tracing to no requirement. Amendment A-1 removes all v0 sources from the tree during P0 and retrieves them from tag v0-vibe-coded on demand, because the P0 exit gate requires a tree of only planned files and porting from the tag forces each ported line to be deliberately reintroduced by a task rather than surviving by inertia.

nodes.label: Build Phases P0–P6
nodes.rationale: P4 is the moment of truth: if the model loses to the grid baseline that is the finding, Constitution II.4 requires publishing it, and P5-P6 proceed unchanged — a well-engineered negative result is a stronger portfolio piece than an unexamined positive claim.

nodes.label: Plan Risk Register
nodes.rationale: Slow collection, FastF1 drift on older seasons, and calibration failure are mitigated; 'model does not beat baseline' is explicitly not a risk but a valid answer the write-up is designed for.

nodes.label: Spec 001 — Core Predictor
nodes.author: Claude (agent)
nodes.rationale: States WHAT the system must do and WHY, with no implementation decisions — a module name or library here belongs in the plan instead.

nodes.label: Ratification Record and Checklist
nodes.rationale: RATIFIED 2026-08-25 by Shiva Kaushik; per IX.3 the drafting agent may not ratify. Ticked entries were verified byte-identical to the text read that day, and entries changed after the read must be re-read before signing — a per-section defence against a material amendment slipping in behind an approval.

nodes.label: Problem Statement — Beat the Grid
nodes.rationale: v0 trained a 50-feature XGBoost ranker and lost to the trivial grid signal on five of six metrics while reporting numbers inflated by post-race weather. The deliverable is a defensible answer whichever way it falls.

nodes.label: User Stories US-1..US-5 and Traceability Map
nodes.rationale: A user story that no requirement serves is decoration, and a requirement that serves no story is scope creep; every story resolves to requirements and to an acceptance criterion that proves it.

nodes.label: Target Variable — Classified Finishing Position (FR-001..003a)
nodes.rationale: Placed first because every metric, the noise floor, and the retirement model are meaningless without it. Matches how F1 itself classifies a race, keeps every starter so field size is constant, and gives retirement an ordered position rather than a sentinel that would fabricate ties. Known accepted cost: a lap-1 collision scores near-worst even for a fast car — real prediction error from real randomness, which is what the noise floor exists to quantify. Raw status is kept verbatim (~30 values per season) so an alternative target needs no recollection.

nodes.label: FR-002 — Withdrawal vs Zero-Lap Retirement
nodes.rationale: Non-start must come from the source's explicit withdrawal marker, never inferred from zero laps: a lap-1 retirement and a car that never started both complete zero laps, and conflating them would delete real races from the corpus.

nodes.label: FR-003a — 'Did Not Finish' Is Not 'Not Classified'
nodes.rationale: A car retiring late having completed enough distance is still classified and still holds a position; classification is derived from the source's position sentinel, not the status string.

nodes.label: Data Acquisition Requirements (FR-1xx)
nodes.rationale: Per-season checkpointing and resume, per-race failure tolerance, chronological ordering fields, row-count sanity warnings, and a bar on committing collected data.

nodes.label: Failure Manifest and Abort Threshold (FR-104a..c)
nodes.rationale: A failed race is excluded whole because a partially collected race silently shrinks a field and corrupts every field-relative feature; it remains a gap rather than a deletion so rolling features treat it as absent and retain their true race counts; and collection aborts past a documented threshold because continuing yields a corpus that looks complete and is not.

nodes.label: Weekend Format Vocabulary (FR-108)
nodes.rationale: The upstream vocabulary is larger than the enum and changed three times (sprint 2021-22, sprint_shootout 2023, sprint_qualifying 2024-25), so an unrecognised raw value is an error rather than a silent fallback to CONVENTIONAL. 'Qualifying result' is not one concept across the corpus: the grid field must be the grid actually started from, never inferred from a qualifying classification.

nodes.label: Circuit Attribute Table (FR-109)
nodes.rationale: Circuit type and overtaking-difficulty tier are declared data maintained alongside the regime table rather than inferred at run time; a missing entry is an error, not a default.

nodes.label: Pagination Completeness Assertion (FR-110)
nodes.rationale: A paginated request returning fewer records than the API says exist looks identical to a complete small season, so completeness is asserted from the reported total and never inferred from a successful HTTP response.

nodes.label: Transient-Failure Retry with Backoff (FR-111)
nodes.rationale: Transient network failure must be distinguished from genuine absence of data; exhausted retries are reported as failures, never recorded as a session that does not exist.

nodes.label: Feature Engineering Requirements (FR-2xx)
nodes.rationale: Machine-readable availability declarations, a primary set of pre-race features only, strictly-prior rolling computation, two automated leakage checks, deterministic builds, and the oracle set as the sole home for post-race features.

nodes.label: Regime-Relative Feature Constraint (FR-209)
nodes.rationale: At a regulation reset absolute pace is destroyed — a 2021 constructor's average finishing position says nothing about its 2022 car — but relative structure persists, because 'P3 on the grid finishes near P3' is a fact about track position and overtaking difficulty, not about which car is quick. team_avg_finish = 4.2 dies at a reset; team_rank_in_field = 2 survives it. This is a constraint on how features are written, not extra machinery.

nodes.label: Declared Regulation Regime Table (FR-210)
nodes.rationale: Regime identity and seasons-elapsed become PRE_RACE features; boundaries are declared data, never inferred from the calendar, because F1 regulation cycles are irregular and no fixed period is correct.

nodes.label: Sprint Result as PRE_RACE Feature (FR-211)
nodes.rationale: A sprint result is knowable before lights out so it satisfies III.1; the feature is explicitly null on conventional weekends rather than imputed with a neutral value that would misrepresent a sprint that never happened.

nodes.label: Cold-Start Fallbacks and LOW_INFORMATION Flag (FR-212)
nodes.rationale: Rookies, new teams and returning entrants take declared fallback values rather than silently propagating nulls, and the prediction is flagged LOW_INFORMATION everywhere. Fallbacks may not be the field mean, which would assert average competitiveness the system has no evidence for.

nodes.label: Telemetry Feature Group as a Separate Arm (FR-213..215)
nodes.rationale: Long-run practice pace and tyre-stint characteristics are drawn only from sessions preceding the race, are explicitly null before 2018 and never imputed, and therefore cover roughly half the 2010-2025 corpus — so they are barred from the primary set and measured as a separate arm on telemetry-covered seasons with the reduced season count stated alongside any benefit.

nodes.label: Driver-Transfer Robustness and POST_TRANSFER Flag (FR-216)
nodes.rationale: Constructor-derived rolling features must not carry the previous constructor's history across a move; driver-derived features carry across unchanged. Learning transfer effects needs data the project lacks, but not inheriting old-team form is a correctness fix rather than a modelling ambition.

nodes.label: Junior-Formula Supplement with Hard Date Filter (FR-217, FR-218)
nodes.rationale: External junior-formula records may supplement cold-start fallbacks only under four conditions: each record carries an event date and is admitted only if it precedes the race; undated records are discarded rather than estimated; source, retrieval date and licence are recorded; and data is cached and version-pinned so determinism survives a source that changes underneath the project. The leakage check is extended to fail on any record dated on or after the race.

nodes.label: Oracle Feature Set (FR-207)
nodes.rationale: An explicitly labelled set including post-race features, usable only for upper-bound analysis and the sole place observed race weather may appear.

nodes.label: Baseline Requirements (FR-3xx)
nodes.rationale: Grid-order, standings-order and a random-order control, all evaluated by the identical code path and metrics on the identical holdout, and reported as first-class citizens rather than a footnote.

nodes.label: Random-Order Control over ≥1000 Seeded Orderings (FR-303)
nodes.rationale: Establishes the random-chance floor as a mean with its own CI; a single draw has variance large enough to make the floor meaningless. Explicitly distinct from the irreducible noise floor of FR-754.

nodes.label: Model Requirements (FR-4xx)
nodes.rationale: Within-race ranking plus point prediction and interval, training strictly prior to holdout, six enumerated metadata fields on every persisted model, seed reproducibility, and configurable recency weighting where uniform weighting stays expressible so its effect is measured rather than assumed.

nodes.label: Evaluation Requirements (FR-5xx)
nodes.rationale: Nine enumerated metrics for model and every baseline, bootstrap CIs on each and on the model-minus-grid delta, segmentation by season, circuit type and overtaking tier so aggregates cannot conceal systematic failure, and an explicit prominent verdict when the model does not beat the grid baseline.

nodes.label: Primary Metric — Spearman Rank Correlation (FR-500)
nodes.rationale: The task is fundamentally ordinal — who finishes ahead of whom, not the arithmetic gap — and position-difference metrics like MAE are dominated by DNF noise under the FR-001 target where a lap-1 retirement lands near the back regardless of pace. Eight other metrics are reported so no single metric can be gamed, but only one may gate a claim.

nodes.label: Fixed-Width Rolling Corpus Window (FR-508..510)
nodes.rationale: F1 relevance decays, so dropping the oldest season as a new one arrives is a modelling decision rather than bookkeeping — but whether recency beats volume is empirical, which is why W may never be hard-coded. W defaults to 16 (2010-2025), advances at both ends when a season completes with all results regenerated, admits completed seasons only, and may never resolve below 8 without failing loudly.

nodes.label: Regulation-Transfer Experiment (FR-511, FR-511a, FR-512)
nodes.rationale: Measures what a regime change costs by comparing a reset season against the season immediately preceding it under an identical protocol, at zero and non-zero decay. It runs over the full collected archive rather than the rolling window because a 16-wide window advancing yearly would push the 2017 transition out of reach from 2028, silently dropping it to DIAGNOSTIC and taking the count back to n=1 with nothing in the output explaining why. Result: two compliant observations (2017, 2022) plus 2014 as a diagnostic, reported as n=2 and never generalised into a rate or law.

nodes.label: Race Simulation Requirements (FR-6xx)
nodes.rationale: Monte Carlo over race outcomes producing a full position distribution per driver, modelling five factors that must match those required by FR-751, emitting win/podium/points probabilities, deterministic given a seed, with per-driver probabilities summing to 1.0 within 1e-6.

nodes.label: Calibration Requirements (FR-7xx)
nodes.rationale: Reliability curves and Brier scores against a climatological base rate and the grid baseline, empirical interval coverage, an UNCALIBRATED label applied at the rendering layer, and a bar on unmeasured probabilities supporting any claim.

nodes.label: Race Randomness Requirements (FR-75x)
nodes.rationale: Implements Article X: five factors modelled as distributions from prior races only, weather kept to exactly two roles, no bare point estimates, at least one proper scoring rule, and error interpreted against the noise floor.

nodes.label: Irreducible Noise Floor Estimation (FR-754)
nodes.rationale: Estimated empirically — variance between races near-identical in all pre-race respects, plus bounding mechanical DNFs and first-lap incidents. The estimate will be crude, but a crude floor is far more informative than comparing model error to zero, which implicitly asserts that a perfect predictor of a chaotic sport could exist.

nodes.label: Interface Requirements (FR-8xx)
nodes.rationale: Six CLI commands; missing upstream artifacts fail with the exact producing command named; grid CSV validation reports all violations at once; and precision rules cap probabilities at two decimals and forbid rendering a metric to more places than its CI half-width supports, because v0 printed win probabilities to four decimals with no evidence any of them meant anything.

nodes.label: Documentation Requirements (FR-9xx)
nodes.rationale: Headline result above any feature list, every number traceable to a committed results file, the v0 leakage defect and its controls documented, non-commercial framing stated, and the full FastF1 provenance and licensing position given.

nodes.label: Non-Functional Requirements (NFR-01..07)
nodes.rationale: 'A developer laptop' is not a specification, so NFR-01 binds the five-minute budget to a named machine plus a recorded measurement; NFR-06 makes a violated declared constraint a defect rather than a warning; NFR-07 forces dependency re-verification at the start of each phase.

nodes.label: Out of Scope Boundaries
nodes.rationale: Each exclusion is a deliberate decision with a stated reason. Two boundaries were deliberately narrowed rather than lifted: transfer robustness is in scope while transfer-effect modelling is not, and regime robustness is in scope while predicting an unraced regime remains excluded because forecasting what 2026's cars will do would be fabrication. Live/in-race prediction stays out because it consumes data the pre-race model cannot have and so cannot move the headline metric.

nodes.label: Acceptance Criteria AC-1..AC-22
nodes.rationale: Defines 'done' objectively, including AC-2's requirement that a deliberately introduced post-race feature must make the leakage check fail, and AC-17's insistence that collection be provably complete rather than merely successful.

nodes.label: Open Questions OQ-1..OQ-7
nodes.rationale: OQ-5, OQ-6 and OQ-7 are closed; OQ-1..4 resolve from data. OQ-1 carries a live caveat: a 2023-25 holdout sits entirely inside the post-2022 ground-effect regime, so the headline number measures within-regime performance and that limitation must be stated wherever the headline result appears.

nodes.label: T-099 Spike Finding — Pre-2018 Data Availability
nodes.rationale: The premise behind OQ-5 was wrong: FastF1's widely-cited 2018 floor applies to lap timing and telemetry, not results. Race results, qualifying, standings and schedule return complete rows from 1996 to 2025, and fastf1 3.8.3 sets BASE_URL to the jolpica Ergast-compatible backend, so the project depends on jolpica transitively. Qualifying format, not availability, is the real constraint on corpus depth. The spike exposed six defects now closed: FR-002 was unimplementable, FR-003's status enum was far too coarse, 'not finished' is not 'not classified' (Bahrain 2022), FR-001 is mostly already satisfied by the source, pagination truncates silently (2 sprints reported instead of 6), and the 5-second default timeout tripped 3 times in ~90 requests.

nodes.label: OQ-6 — Corpus Starts in 2010
nodes.rationale: Resolved by the owner 2026-08-25. 2010 is the first season after the refuelling ban, so every grid in the corpus was set on low fuel and means what a modern grid means — which matters because the project's whole question is whether a model can beat the grid. A 2006 start would have bought a third transition at the cost of four seasons whose Q3 ran on race fuel, contaminating the very baseline the project is measured against. Gives a 16-season corpus, FR-511 n=2 compliant plus one diagnostic, and retires the FR-511a exemption.

nodes.label: Tasks 001 — Core Predictor Board
nodes.rationale: Board rules per Constitution VII: a task with no requirement ID in Satisfies is out of scope and gets deleted; a task is done when its 'Done when' clause is objectively true, not when the code works; and if implementing a task shows the spec is wrong, the spec is amended first.

nodes.label: Phase P0 — Cull
nodes.rationale: COMPLETE 2026-08-15: 24 files deleted, package skeleton created, dependencies pinned, results/ tracked. Exit gate is that the repository contains only what plan §5 retains — nothing else.

nodes.label: Phase P1 — Data Acquisition
nodes.rationale: T-106 runs early because it answers the project's highest-severity risk and nothing downstream should be built before its answer is known. Exit gate AC-1 and AC-11, also closing OQ-1 and OQ-5.

nodes.label: T-099 — Pre-2018 Results Availability Spike
nodes.rationale: DONE 2026-08-24. Answer: yes, back to 1996. Spike deleted per VII.1a with its finding recorded in spec §7.1; closed OQ-5, opened the OQ-6 corpus-start decision, and exposed six defects now closed as FR-001a, FR-003, FR-003a, FR-108, FR-110, FR-111.

nodes.label: T-106 — Collect 16 Seasons 2010–2025
nodes.rationale: Sixteen seasons present per the resolved OQ-6 2010 start, per-season counts reported, shortfall recorded if any; 2026 excluded because it is in progress.

nodes.label: T-108 — Implement CorpusWindow Resolution
nodes.rationale: W defaults to 16 and is configurable, resolves to 2010-2025 as of 2025, an in-progress season provably cannot enter, and it is unit-tested with a frozen clock either side of a season boundary.

nodes.label: Phase P2 — Feature Registry & Leakage Firewall
nodes.rationale: Exit gate AC-2, where T-207 is 'the gate's gate' — an untested test is not a control.

nodes.label: T-207 — Negative Control Test
nodes.rationale: A deliberately leaky feature must make both the static and the behavioural leakage check fail, proving the controls actually fire.

nodes.label: Phase P3 — Baselines & Evaluation Harness
nodes.rationale: Baselines are evaluated here, before the model exists, so the bar is set before there is any temptation to move it.

nodes.label: Phase P4 — Model
nodes.rationale: Exit gate AC-4 and AC-12: the headline answer exists and is committed whichever way it falls, as does the measured cost of a regulation reset.

nodes.label: T-409 — Regulation-Transfer Experiment
nodes.rationale: Run over the full archive rather than the FR-508 window for all three resets against their preceding-season comparators, at two decay settings, each carrying its actual training-season count, with 2014 labelled DIAGNOSTIC and the headline stated as n=2.

nodes.label: Phase P5 — Simulation & Calibration
nodes.rationale: Exit gate AC-5 and AC-6; includes T-514's assertion that no output path can emit a position without an interval.

nodes.label: T-512 — Estimate Irreducible Noise Floor
nodes.rationale: Floor committed to results/ with its method documented, resolving OQ-4's choice of estimator.

nodes.label: Phase P6 — Interface & Write-up
nodes.rationale: Exit gate AC-7 and AC-8; includes T-611's requirement that the README state the within-regime caveat wherever the headline number appears.

nodes.label: Requirement-to-Task Traceability Check
nodes.rationale: Every requirement group maps to at least one task: no orphan requirements, no orphan tasks. This is the mechanical enforcement of Constitution VII.2.

nodes.label: Spec Amendments Log
nodes.rationale: Per VII.3 the spec is amended before the code diverges, and each entry records what forced the change — adversarial review finding the target variable undefined, FR-511 mandating training arms that contradicted FR-501's floor, unfalsifiable requirements like 'a developer laptop' violating VII.4, and the T-099 spike closing six defects at once.

nodes.label: Owner-Action Flag on Constitution X.1
nodes.rationale: When weather was added as a fifth randomness factor, the log recorded that Constitution X.1 needed the same amendment and marked it explicitly as owner action, not the agent's — the agent may not amend the document that governs it.
